objects.description: No types are defined in this header. It only aggregates other headers (config.h, json_features.h, reader.h, value.h, writer.h). Json::Value is a common type from JsonCpp but it is not defined in this file; therefore it should not be included per the instructions. This placeholder entry indicates that there are no custom data types explicitly defined here.

A deprecated JSON text parser that reads UTF-8 input and produces a Json::Value tree, with optional comment collection. Provides error reporting, including structured errors with byte offsets. Includes internal tokenization helpers and error recovery. Prefer CharReader/CharReaderBuilder for new code.
Error record used by Json::Reader containing byte offsets into the input and a message.

Abstract interface for parsing JSON from a character range into a Json::Value. Supports formatted and structured error reporting. Instances are created via a Factory (e.g., CharReaderBuilder). Provides a protected Impl interface for concrete implementations.
Structured error record used by CharReader reporting byte offsets and message.
Abstract factory for producing CharReader instances via newCharReader().
Concrete factory for creating CharReader implementations. Exposes a Json::Value settings_ object to configure parsing behavior and provides helpers to set defaults and strict modes.

Abstract interface for streaming JSON writers. Holds a non-owning pointer to an output stream during write(). Subclasses implement write() to serialize a Json::Value to the provided OStream. Also defines a nested abstract Factory for constructing StreamWriter instances.
Abstract factory for creating StreamWriter instances. Implementations validate settings and allocate writers via operator new.
Concrete factory for building configured StreamWriter implementations. Stores configuration in settings_ (a Json::Value) and provides helpers to validate, mutate, and reset defaults.
Deprecated abstract base class that serializes a Json::Value to a String in one shot. Superseded by StreamWriter API.
Deprecated, unformatted JSON writer producing a single-line JSON string quickly. Supports YAML-compatibility spacing, omitting null placeholders, and omitting the trailing newline.
Deprecated pretty-printing writer that formats JSON with indentation, line breaks, and comment handling, returning the result as a String.
Deprecated pretty-printing writer that outputs formatted JSON directly to an output stream with configurable indentation. Similar to StyledWriter but stream-oriented.
Base exception type thrown by JsonCpp. Stores a message and overrides what().
Exception for runtime errors that users cannot easily avoid (e.g., resource failures). Derived from Json::Exception.
Exception for precondition violations or internal logic errors. Derived from Json::Exception.
Enumeration of all JSON value kinds representable by Json::Value.
Placement options for comments associated with a Value.
Controls formatting of real numbers as strings: either by significant digits or decimal places.
Lightweight wrapper tagging a const char* as static storage to avoid duplication when used as a key or string Value.

Primary discriminated-union type representing any JSON value (null, bool, integer, floating, string, array, object). Provides rich API for access, mutation, iteration, comments, and metadata. Manages its own storage; arrays/objects are dynamic.
Represents one step in a JSON path: either an array index or an object key. Used to parameterize Path expansion.
A light parser/executor for dotted/bracket JSON path strings, supporting parameterized segments via PathArgument. Can resolve or create nodes in a Value tree.
Abstract base providing common behavior for const and non-const iterators over Json::Value arrays/objects.
Read-only iterator for traversing elements or members of a Json::Value.
Mutable iterator for traversing and modifying elements or members of a Json::Value.

objects.definition: typedef std::map<CZString, Value> ObjectValues;
objects.description: Map type used internally by Json::Value to store object members keyed by CZString.

Configuration class (namespace Json) used to control JsonCpp reader/writer behavior. Provides defaults via constructor and two factory-like static methods: all() for permissive parsing and strictMode() for spec-compliant behavior. Public data members toggle comment allowance, root strictness, acceptance of dropped null placeholders, and numeric keys. Construction is default; destruction is trivial. JSON_API is a visibility macro; there is no custom memory management indicated.

objects.definition: class StreamWriter;
objects.description: Forward declaration of a JSON writer interface that streams output. Only declared here; no members available in this header.

objects.definition: class StreamWriterBuilder;
objects.description: Forward-declared builder for constructing StreamWriter instances with configurable options.

objects.definition: class Writer;
objects.description: Forward-declared abstract JSON writer base class. Specific writer implementations derive from this.

objects.definition: class FastWriter;
objects.description: Forward-declared concrete Writer that produces JSON without extra formatting for speed.

objects.definition: class StyledWriter;
objects.description: Forward-declared pretty-printing JSON writer that formats output with indentation and newlines.

objects.definition: class StyledStreamWriter;

objects.definition: class Features;
objects.description: Forward-declared configuration object describing enabled/disabled JSON reader features.

objects.definition: using ArrayIndex = unsigned int;
objects.description: Type alias used for indexing arrays in Json::Value. This is an alias; no additional semantics are defined here.

objects.definition: class StaticString;

objects.definition: class Path;

objects.definition: class ValueConstIterator;
objects.description: Forward-declared const iterator over Json::Value children (arrays/objects).
Alias for built-in int used throughout JsonCpp to represent signed integers.
Alias for unsigned int used for non-negative integer values in JsonCpp.
Alias for a 64-bit signed integer type, mapped to platform-appropriate underlying type. Present only when JSON_NO_INT64 is not defined.
Alias for a 64-bit unsigned integer type, mapped to platform-appropriate underlying type. Present only when JSON_NO_INT64 is not defined.
Alias for the widest signed integer type supported by the library (either int or Int64 depending on configuration).
Alias for the widest unsigned integer type supported by the library (either unsigned int or UInt64 depending on configuration).
Primary string type used by JsonCpp, a std::basic_string<char> specialized with Json::Allocator<char>.
Input string stream type compatible with Json::String’s character traits and allocator.
Output string stream type compatible with Json::String’s character traits and allocator.
Alias for std::istream used by the library.
Alias for std::ostream used by the library.

This header defines only preprocessor macros for JsonCpp versioning and a configuration macro for secure memory. It does not declare or define any structs, enums, classes, or typedefs. Therefore, there are no custom data types to document.

functions.name: Json::Reader::Reader
functions.description: Default constructor for the legacy Json::Reader parser (deprecated). Constructs a Reader instance with all parsing features enabled.
requirements: Deprecated: Prefer Json::CharReader and Json::CharReaderBuilder instead.

functions.name: Json::Reader::Reader
functions.description: Constructs a legacy Json::Reader (deprecated) configured with the specified feature set.
requirements: Deprecated: Prefer Json::CharReader and Json::CharReaderBuilder instead.
The Json::Features object must be properly initialized with desired options before construction.

functions.name: Json::Reader::parse
functions.signature: bool Json::Reader::parse(const std::string& document, Json::Value& root, bool collectComments = true)
functions.description: Parses a UTF-8 JSON document from a std::string into 'root'. Returns true on success, false on failure. Optionally collects and preserves comments.
requirements: Input 'document' must be UTF-8 encoded.
If 'collectComments' is true, comments are collected unless disabled by the feature set (ignored if Features::allowComments_ is false).
On success, 'root' contains the parsed JSON value; on failure, it is unspecified and errors can be queried via getFormattedErrorMessages() or getStructuredErrors().

functions.name: Json::Reader::parse
functions.signature: bool Json::Reader::parse(const char* beginDoc, const char* endDoc, Json::Value& root, bool collectComments = true)
functions.description: Parses a UTF-8 JSON document from a character range [beginDoc, endDoc) into 'root'. Returns true on success, false on failure. Optionally collects and preserves comments.
requirements: 'beginDoc' must point to the start of the UTF-8 document.
'endDoc' must be >= 'beginDoc' and point one past the last byte of the document.
If 'collectComments' is true, comments are collected unless disabled by the feature set (ignored if Features::allowComments_ is false).
On success, 'root' contains the parsed JSON value; on failure, it is unspecified and errors can be queried via getFormattedErrorMessages() or getStructuredErrors().

functions.name: Json::Reader::parse
functions.signature: bool Json::Reader::parse(IStream& is, Json::Value& root, bool collectComments = true)
functions.description: Parses a JSON value from an input stream into 'root'. Returns true on success, false on failure. Optionally collects and preserves comments.
requirements: The input stream must provide the JSON text (encoding expectation is UTF-8 by convention of Reader).
If 'collectComments' is true, comments are collected unless disabled by the feature set (ignored if Features::allowComments_ is false).
On success, 'root' contains the parsed JSON value; on failure, it is unspecified and errors can be queried via getFormattedErrorMessages() or getStructuredErrors().

functions.name: Json::Reader::getFormatedErrorMessages
functions.description: Returns a human-friendly string listing parse errors and their locations. Deprecated in favor of getFormattedErrorMessages() (typo fix). Empty string if no errors occurred.
requirements: Deprecated: Use getFormattedErrorMessages() instead.

functions.name: Json::Reader::getFormattedErrorMessages
functions.description: Returns a human-friendly string listing parse errors and their locations from the last parse attempt. Empty string if no errors occurred.

functions.name: Json::Reader::getStructuredErrors
functions.description: Returns a vector of structured parse errors (offset range and message) from the last parse attempt. The vector may be empty. Multiple errors should be tolerated by callers.

functions.name: Json::Reader::pushError
functions.signature: bool Json::Reader::pushError(const Json::Value& value, const Json::String& message)
functions.description: Adds a semantic error associated with a particular JSON value location. Returns true if the error was recorded.
requirements: Returns false if the Value's offset exceeds the document size.

functions.name: Json::Reader::pushError
functions.signature: bool Json::Reader::pushError(const Json::Value& value, const Json::String& message, const Json::Value& extra)
functions.description: Adds a semantic error associated with a particular JSON value location, with extra contextual location. Returns true if the error was recorded.
requirements: Returns false if either Value's offset exceeds the document size.

functions.name: Json::Reader::good
functions.description: Indicates whether there are no errors to report from the last parse. Returns true if no errors have occurred, false otherwise.

functions.name: Json::CharReader::~CharReader
functions.description: Virtual destructor for Json::CharReader interface. Enables proper cleanup via base-class pointer.

functions.name: Json::CharReader::parse
functions.signature: virtual bool Json::CharReader::parse(char const* beginDoc, char const* endDoc, Json::Value* root, Json::String* errs)
functions.description: Parses a UTF-8 JSON document from the range [beginDoc, endDoc) into '*root'. On success returns true; on failure returns false and optionally fills '*errs' with formatted error messages.
requirements: 'beginDoc' must point to the start of the UTF-8 document.
'endDoc' must be >= 'beginDoc' and point one past the last byte of the document.
'root' must be a non-null pointer to a Json::Value to receive the result.
'errs' may be NULL; if non-null, it receives human-friendly error messages on failure.
Each call may reset the internal list of structured errors retrievable via getStructuredErrors().

functions.name: Json::CharReader::getStructuredErrors
functions.description: Returns a vector of structured errors (offsets and message) collected during the last parse. Each parse call resets the stored list.
requirements: Call after parse() to inspect errors from that parse; earlier results are reset on each parse call.

functions.name: Json::CharReader::Factory::~Factory
functions.description: Virtual destructor for Json::CharReader::Factory, enabling deletion via base pointer.

functions.name: Json::CharReader::Factory::newCharReader
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new CharReader instance. Implementations may throw on invalid settings.
requirements: May throw std::exception if something goes wrong (e.g., invalid settings). Callers should be prepared to handle exceptions.
Caller owns the returned pointer and must delete it when no longer needed (unless using a smart pointer).

functions.name: Json::CharReaderBuilder::CharReaderBuilder
functions.description: Constructs a CharReaderBuilder with default parsing settings stored in 'settings_'. Settings are case-sensitive and can be modified via operator[].

functions.name: Json::CharReaderBuilder::~CharReaderBuilder
functions.description: Destructor for CharReaderBuilder.

functions.name: Json::CharReaderBuilder::newCharReader
functions.description: Creates a new CharReader configured according to this builder's settings. Ownership of the returned pointer is transferred to the caller.
requirements: May throw if settings are invalid (by contract of Factory::newCharReader()).
Caller must delete the returned CharReader (or manage it with a smart pointer).

functions.name: Json::CharReaderBuilder::validate
functions.description: Validates the builder's 'settings_' for legality and consistency. Returns true if settings are valid; otherwise returns false and indicates bad settings via '*invalid'.
requirements: If provided, 'invalid' should be a non-null pointer to a Json::Value to receive details about invalid settings.

functions.name: Json::CharReaderBuilder::operator[]
functions.description: Provides access to a specific builder setting by name, allowing read/write. Keys are case-sensitive.
requirements: 'key' is case-sensitive; use documented key names exactly as specified in the comments (e.g., "collectComments", "allowComments", etc.).

functions.name: Json::CharReaderBuilder::setDefaults
functions.description: Sets default parsing settings into '*settings'. Can also be used to reset settings.
requirements: Precondition: 'settings' must not be NULL (a Json::null value is acceptable).
Caller must supply a valid Json::Value pointer to receive defaults.

functions.name: Json::CharReaderBuilder::strictMode
functions.description: Configures '*settings' to strict mode (equivalent to the old Features::strictMode()).
requirements: Precondition: 'settings' must not be NULL (a Json::null value is acceptable).

functions.name: Json::CharReaderBuilder::ecma404Mode
functions.description: Configures '*settings' for ECMA-404 mode.
requirements: Precondition: 'settings' must not be NULL (a Json::null value is acceptable).

functions.name: Json::parseFromStream
functions.signature: bool Json::parseFromStream(Json::CharReader::Factory const& factory, IStream& is, Json::Value* root, Json::String* errs)
functions.description: Consumes the entire input stream and parses a JSON value using a CharReader produced by 'factory'. On success stores the result into '*root' and returns true; on failure returns false and may fill '*errs' with messages.
requirements: 'factory' must be a valid CharReader factory capable of producing a reader for the desired settings.
'root' should point to a valid Json::Value to receive the parsed result.
The function consumes the entire stream content as input.

functions.name: Json::operator>>
functions.description: Extracts JSON from an input stream into 'root'. Always preserves comments from the input JSON. Throws std::exception on parse error.
requirements: Caller must handle exceptions: this function throws std::exception on parse error.
Can be used to read into a sub-object (e.g., root["dir"]["file"]).

functions.name: Json::StreamWriter::StreamWriter
functions.description: Default constructor for the abstract JSON stream writer. Initializes internal state; the output stream (sout_) is not owned and is supplied per-call to write().
requirements: None beyond standard object construction. The output stream is provided to write() and is not owned by the writer.

functions.name: Json::StreamWriter::~StreamWriter
functions.description: Virtual destructor for StreamWriter. Ensures proper cleanup through base-class pointers.
requirements: Do not assume the writer owns any stream passed to write(); callers must manage the lifetime of any OStream passed to write().

functions.name: Json::StreamWriter::write

functions.description: Pure-virtual function to serialize a JSON Value to the provided output stream according to the concrete writer’s configuration.
requirements: sout must not be NULL (precondition).
Caller retains ownership of sout and must ensure it remains valid for the duration of the call.
Return value is zero on success; callers should check the stream state to detect errors.
May throw std::exception depending on configuration; callers should be prepared to handle exceptions.

functions.name: Json::StreamWriter::Factory::~Factory
functions.description: Virtual destructor for the StreamWriter abstract factory, enabling safe deletion via base-class pointer.
requirements: None.

functions.name: Json::StreamWriter::Factory::newStreamWriter

May throw std::exception if something goes wrong (e.g., invalid settings); callers should handle exceptions.

functions.name: Json::StreamWriterBuilder::setDefaults

functions.name: Json::FastWriter::FastWriter

functions.name: Json::SecureAllocator::allocate
functions.description: Allocates raw, uninitialized storage for n objects of type T using the global operator new. Intended for use as the allocator’s allocate operation. Returns a T* to the beginning of the allocated block.
requirements: n is the number of T objects to allocate; the total size is n * sizeof(T).
Behavior follows global operator new; allocation may throw std::bad_alloc on failure.
The caller must subsequently construct objects in the returned storage before use (e.g., via construct).
The caller is responsible for eventually releasing the memory with deallocate using the same allocator type and the same n.

functions.name: Json::SecureAllocator::deallocate
functions.description: Securely releases storage previously allocated for n objects of type T. The memory is zeroed before being freed via the global operator delete.
requirements: p must point to a block previously obtained from Json::SecureAllocator<T>::allocate (or an equivalent allocation for T) and not yet deallocated.
n must be the same number of T objects that were originally requested for this allocation.
p must be valid and suitably aligned for T; passing an invalid pointer results in undefined behavior.
If n is greater than 0, p must be non-null to avoid zeroing via a null pointer.
This function does not invoke destructors; destroy T objects before calling deallocate if they were constructed.

functions.name: Json::SecureAllocator::construct
functions.signature:
template <typename... Args>
void Json::SecureAllocator<T>::construct(T* p, Args&&... args)
functions.description: Constructs a T object in-place at address p using placement new and perfect-forwarded constructor arguments.
requirements: p must point to suitably aligned, uninitialized storage large enough for a T (typically obtained from allocate).
The forwarded arguments args must match a valid constructor of T; construction may throw exceptions as per T’s constructor.
Do not call construct on the same storage more than once without destroying the previous object.
After successful construction, destroy must be called before deallocating the storage.

functions.name: Json::SecureAllocator::max_size
functions.description: Returns the maximum number of T objects that could theoretically be allocated by this allocator on the current platform, computed as size_t(-1) / sizeof(T).
requirements: None beyond a valid allocator object.

functions.name: Json::SecureAllocator::address
functions.description: Returns the address of the referenced T object x (equivalent to std::addressof(x)).
requirements: x must be a valid T object.

functions.name: Json::SecureAllocator::address
functions.signature: const T* Json::SecureAllocator<T>::address(const T& x) const
functions.description: Returns the address of the referenced const T object x (equivalent to std::addressof(x)).
requirements: x must be a valid T object.

functions.name: Json::SecureAllocator::destroy
functions.description: Destroys the T object located at p by explicitly invoking its destructor. Does not deallocate memory.
requirements: p must point to a live T object previously constructed in the storage.
Do not pass null or an invalid pointer; doing so is undefined behavior.
After destroy, the storage may be reused for a new construction or released via deallocate.

functions.name: Json::SecureAllocator::SecureAllocator
functions.description: Default constructor for the SecureAllocator. Performs no stateful initialization.
requirements: None.

functions.name: Json::SecureAllocator::SecureAllocator
functions.description: Converting (rebind) constructor that allows constructing a SecureAllocator<T> from a SecureAllocator<U>. Enables allocator propagation across different value types.
requirements: The source allocator must be a valid Json::SecureAllocator<U>.
No additional state is copied; construction is noexcept by structure (unknown if declared noexcept).

functions.name: Json::operator==
functions.signature:
template <typename T, typename U>
bool Json::operator==(const Json::SecureAllocator<T>&, const Json::SecureAllocator<U>&)
functions.description: Compares two SecureAllocator instances for equality. Always returns true, meaning all SecureAllocator instances are considered interchangeable.
requirements: None; valid SecureAllocator operands.

functions.name: Json::operator!=

template <typename T, typename U>
bool Json::operator!=(const Json::SecureAllocator<T>&, const Json::SecureAllocator<U>&)
functions.description: Compares two SecureAllocator instances for inequality. Always returns false, meaning no two SecureAllocator instances are considered unequal.
requirements: None; valid SecureAllocator operands.

functions.name: Json::Features::all
functions.description: Returns a Features configuration that enables all permissive parsing/writing features and assumes UTF-8 strings. Typical usage: pass the returned Features to a Json reader/writer to allow C/C++-style comments, permit any JSON value as the root, and treat strings as UTF-8.
requirements: No arguments required.
Returned object should be supplied to Json reader/writer components that accept a Features configuration.
Thread-safety and lifetime semantics are not documented; treat the returned Features as a value object to be copied or moved as needed.

functions.name: Json::Features::strictMode
functions.description: Returns a Features configuration that conforms strictly to the JSON specification. Typical usage: pass the returned Features to a Json reader/writer to forbid comments, require the root to be an array or object, and assume UTF-8 strings.
requirements: No arguments required.
Returned object should be supplied to Json reader/writer components that accept a Features configuration.
Strict mode implies: comments are not allowed; the root value must be an array or object; strings are assumed UTF-8.

functions.name: Json::Features::Features
functions.description: Default constructor initializing a Features configuration similar to JsonConfig::allFeatures per the comment. The in-class defaults are: allowComments_ = true, strictRoot_ = false, allowDroppedNullPlaceholders_ = false, allowNumericKeys_ = false. Construct and then optionally modify flags before passing to a Json reader/writer.
requirements: No arguments required.
Object must be initialized (constructed) before use.
Caller may modify the public flags (allowComments_, strictRoot_, allowDroppedNullPlaceholders_, allowNumericKeys_) prior to passing to other APIs.
Exact parity with JsonConfig::allFeatures is noted in comment but details beyond listed default members are not documented.

functions.name: msvc_pre1900_c99_snprintf
functions.signature: extern JSON_API int msvc_pre1900_c99_snprintf(char* outBuf, size_t size, const char* format, ...);
functions.description: Compatibility wrapper providing a C99-like snprintf for Microsoft Visual C++ compilers older than MSVC 2015 (_MSC_VER < 1900). It is used internally via the jsoncpp_snprintf macro on those platforms. Call it like snprintf: pass an output buffer, its size in bytes, a printf-style format string, and corresponding variadic arguments. Exact return-value semantics (C99 vs. MSVC) are not documented here; it is intended to mimic C99 snprintf behavior, but details are unknown from this header.
requirements: Only available/used when compiling with MSVC and _MSC_VER < 1900; on other compilers jsoncpp_snprintf maps to std::snprintf and this symbol may not be linked.
outBuf should point to a writable buffer of at least 'size' bytes; passing an invalid or insufficient buffer can cause undefined behavior (inferred from snprintf-style API).
size should be the total capacity of outBuf in bytes (inferred from snprintf-style API).
format must be a non-null, valid printf-style format string (inferred from snprintf-style API).
Variadic arguments must match the format specifiers in 'format' (inferred from printf conventions).
Callers should check the returned int to detect errors or truncation; exact conventions (negative on error vs. required size) are not specified in this header and thus are unknown.

Arbitrary string data with no specific format requirements. May include any bytes/characters; not required to be structured or encoded in a specific way beyond being representable as a C/C++ string.

generators.generator:
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target domain: free-form text used as std::string inputs to exercise JsonCpp APIs in stubs.
# We want valid, interesting UTF-8 friendly strings that cover:
# - Small/medium sizes (kept <= 4096 overall)
# - JSON-like snippets (objects, arrays, numbers, strings, booleans, null)
# - Keys and values with diverse characters (ASCII, Unicode, escape sequences)
# - Comment-looking substrings (//, /* */) for readers that may collect comments
# - Strings with embedded NULs are generally unsafe for C-strings in some APIs in the stubs,
#   so we avoid embedding actual NUL bytes. We can still include edge whitespace and control chars.
# - Paths/keys for object operations, short to moderate length
# - Error messages for Exception/pushError
# - Keep typical lengths small to increase chance that offsets (0..512) fall within string length
#
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR in the stubs is used for:
# - Json::Reader::pushError message
# - StyledWriter/StyledStreamWriter values (text, msg)
# - valueToQuotedString input C-string
# - Json::Value default/string elements, keys for find/demand/findNull
# Therefore strings should be valid UTF-8 and reasonable size.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

_ascii_punct = "!@#$%^&*()-_=+[]{}|;:',.<>/?`~"
_ws = " \t\r\n"

# Some reusable interesting snippets
JSON_SNIPPETS = [
    '{"alpha":1,"text":"hello"}',
    '{"a": [1, 2, 3], "b": {"c": true, "d": null}}',
    '[{"id":0},{"id":1},{"id":2}]',
    ' // comment\n{"k": "v"}\n/* block */',
    '{"unicode":"Привет мир – こんにちは世界 – مرحبا"}',
    '{"escapes":"\\b\\f\\n\\r\\t\\\\\""}',
    '{"big":1234567890,"neg":-42,"real":3.14159}',
]

UNICODE_SAMPLES = [
    "café", "naïve", "résumé", "😊", "🐍", "中文测试", "Русский", "عربي", "हिन्दी",
    "𝔘𝔫𝔦𝔠𝔬𝔡𝔢", "ėščŧ", "ąęįųū", "¿Qué tal?", "Γειά σου", "שלום", "한국어"
]

KEY_PREFIXES = ["key", "name", "id", "path", "user", "msg", "alpha", "beta", "γ", "ключ", "路径"]


def rand_choice(rng: random.Random, arr: List[str]) -> str:
    return arr[rng.randrange(len(arr))]


def rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + _ascii_punct + _ws
    return ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))


def rand_unicode(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    # Build from ASCII + UNICODE_SAMPLES chunks to keep valid UTF-8
    parts = []
    target = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    while len(''.join(parts)) < target:
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            parts.append(rand_ascii(rng, 1, 4))
        else:
            parts.append(rand_choice(rng, UNICODE_SAMPLES))
    s = ''.join(parts)
    # trim to target length in characters (safe for BMP samples)
    return s[:target]


def make_json_like(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate a small JSON object with a couple keys
    obj = {}
    # 2-5 keys
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5)):
        key = rand_choice(rng, KEY_PREFIXES)
        # add some variation
        if rng.random() < 0.4:
            key += '_' + str(rng.randint(0, 999))
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            key += rand_choice(rng, ["-x", ":y", "/z"])
        # values of mixed types
        t = rng.random()
        if t < 0.2:
            val = rng.randint(-1000, 1000)
        elif t < 0.4:
            val = rng.random() * (1000 if rng.random() < 0.5 else 1)
        elif t < 0.6:
            val = True if rng.random() < 0.5 else False
        elif t < 0.8:
            val = None
        else:
            # string with escapes and unicode
            base = rand_unicode(rng, 3, 24)
            base = base.replace('"', '\\"').replace('\\', '\\\\')
            val = base
        obj[key] = val
    # Serialize simply
    import json
    return json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False)


def make_key(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    base = rand_choice(rng, KEY_PREFIXES)
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        base += '_' + rand_ascii(rng, 1, 6).strip()
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        base += rand_choice(rng, ["/", ":", ".", "[0]", "-", "::"])  # interesting tokens
    return base.strip() or base


def make_message(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Error/message string: include words, numbers, punctuation, and comment-like pieces
    parts = []
    parts.append(rand_choice(rng, ["error", "warning", "info", "note", "debug"]))
    parts.append(":")
    parts.append(rand_unicode(rng, 5, 20))
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append(" at ")
        parts.append(str(rng.randint(0, 512)))
        parts.append(":")
        parts.append(str(rng.randint(0, 512)))
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        parts.append(" // hint")
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        parts.append(" /* ctx */")
    s = ''.join(parts)
    # limit message length
    if len(s) > 300:
        s = s[:300]
    return s


def make_value_string(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Used where a generic string value is expected
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.25:
        return rand_choice(rng, JSON_SNIPPETS)
    elif choice < 0.5:
        return make_json_like(rng)
    elif choice < 0.75:
        return rand_unicode(rng, 1, 64)
    else:
        s = rand_ascii(rng, 1, 64)
        # include quotes/backslashes sometimes to exercise escaping
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            s = s.replace('\\', '\\\\').replace('"', '\\"')
        return s


def assemble_corpus(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Build a list of strings to be consumed by FUZZ_PARAM_STR across calls.
    corpus: List[str] = []
    # Seed with several JSON-like and free-form strings
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 6)):
        corpus.append(make_value_string(rng))
    # Add some candidate keys for object operations
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5)):
        corpus.append(make_key(rng))
    # Add a couple error messages
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 4)):
        corpus.append(make_message(rng))
    # Ensure presence of small and medium strings
    corpus.append(rand_unicode(rng, 1, 8))
    corpus.append(rand_unicode(rng, 20, 80))
    # Add a long-ish but capped message used in StyledStreamWriter (they cap to 512)
    long_part = rand_unicode(rng, 200, 400)
    corpus.append(long_part)
    # De-duplicate while preserving order (best effort)
    seen = set()
    uniq = []
    for s in corpus:
        if s not in seen:
            seen.add(s)
            uniq.append(s)
    return uniq


def pack_strings(strings: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # Simple length-prefixed concatenation: [count][len][data]...
    # count: 2 bytes little-endian, len: 2 bytes little-endian
    # Data are UTF-8 encoded without NULs inserted by us.
    out = bytearray()
    count = min(len(strings), 512)
    out += count.to_bytes(2, 'little')
    for s in strings[:count]:
        b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
        if len(b) > 1024:
            b = b[:1024]
        out += len(b).to_bytes(2, 'little')
        out += b
        if len(out) > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
    # Trim to MAX_TOTAL
    return bytes(out[:MAX_TOTAL])


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    strings = assemble_corpus(rng)
    return pack_strings(strings)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target format: "alphanumeric string" intended for keys or indentation.
# Fuzzer stubs use FUZZ_PARAM_STR() for:
# - StreamWriterBuilder::operator[] keys/values (indentation string)
# - StyledStreamWriter indentation string
# - Json::Value::find* member-name lookups
# Our goal: provide a bytes buffer that, when split/consumed by the fuzzer as strings,
# yields interesting yet valid values covering:
# - Common JSON writer settings keys
# - Indentation patterns (tabs, spaces, mixed, ASCII-safe)
# - Object member names that map to various value types for find* lookups
# The buffer is a concatenation of multiple NUL-terminated strings so FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# can slice them deterministically from the buffer.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

COMMON_KEYS = [
    "indentation",
    "commentStyle",
    "enableYAMLCompatibility",
    "dropNullPlaceholders",
    "precision",
    "precisionType",
]

# Member names to exercise find* APIs. The harness will look up keys in a Json::Value
# object created elsewhere; we just provide likely names to increase hit rate.
FIND_KEYS = [
    # booleans
    "flag", "enabled", "active", "isReady",
    # ints
    "count", "retries", "max", "min",
    # int64
    "big", "epoch", "uid",
    # uint
    "uCount", "uMax",
    # uint64
    "uBig", "size",
    # double/numeric
    "ratio", "threshold", "temperature", "value",
    # string
    "name", "title", "message", "desc",
    # array
    "items", "list", "entries",
    # object
    "config", "settings", "meta",
]

INDENT_SAMPLES = [
    "\t",
    " ",
    "  ",
    "    ",
    " \t",
    "\t ",
    ".-",
    "| ",
]

# Small helper to make a C-style NUL-terminated byte string
def to_cstr(s: str) -> bytes:
    return s.encode('utf-8', 'strict') + b"\x00"


def _rand_ident(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=12) -> str:
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-"
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))


def _build_strings(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    out: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Provide a rotation of known builder keys to maximize valid paths
    keys = COMMON_KEYS.copy()
    rng.shuffle(keys)
    for k in keys:
        out.append(to_cstr(k))

    # 2) Provide indentation variants (<= 8 chars as required by stub)
    inds = INDENT_SAMPLES.copy()
    # Add some random short indents
    for _ in range(4):
        s = _rand_ident(rng, 1, 8)
        # bias to spaces/tabs
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            s = (" " * rng.randint(1, 4)) + ("\t" * rng.randint(0, 2))
        inds.append(s[:8])
    rng.shuffle(inds)
    for ind in inds:
        out.append(to_cstr(ind))

    # 3) Provide lookup keys for find* methods
    keys3 = FIND_KEYS.copy()
    # include duplicates and random identifiers to widen surface
    for _ in range(10):
        keys3.append(_rand_ident(rng, 3, 10))
    rng.shuffle(keys3)
    for k in keys3:
        out.append(to_cstr(k))

    # 4) Add some likely values to be used when the fuzzer reuses FUZZ_PARAM_STR
    # for setting values like indentation or commentStyle (e.g., "All").
    extra_vals = ["All", "None", "Minimal", "   ", "\t\t", "0", "1", "2", "9"]
    rng.shuffle(extra_vals)
    for v in extra_vals:
        out.append(to_cstr(v))

    return out


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    chunks = _build_strings(rng)

    # Concatenate until we approach MAX_TOTAL
    buf = bytearray()
    for c in chunks:
        if len(buf) + len(c) > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        buf.extend(c)

    # Ensure non-empty buffer; include at least one indentation and one key if needed
    if not buf:
        buf.extend(to_cstr("indentation"))
        buf.extend(to_cstr("\t"))

    return bytes(buf)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generates valid source-code comment text payloads to be embedded into either
# // line comments or /* block comments */ by the fuzzer stub.
# The stub constructs the final comment string itself, so our payload should be
# interesting but not break validity when wrapped as:
#   // <payload>
# or
#   /* <payload> */
# Therefore, when targeting block comments, avoid introducing the terminator */
# inside payload; when targeting line comments, embedded newlines are fine.

MAX_SIZE = 4096

LINE_ENDINGS = ["\n", "\r\n", "\r"]

def _rand_identifier(r: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=12) -> str:
    first = r.choice(string.ascii_letters + "_")
    rest_len = r.randint(min_len - 1, max_len - 1)
    rest_chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_"
    rest = "".join(r.choice(rest_chars) for _ in range(max(0, rest_len)))
    return first + rest

def _weighted_choice(r: random.Random, items: List[str], weights: List[int]) -> str:
    total = sum(weights)
    x = r.randint(1, total)
    s = 0
    for item, w in zip(items, weights):
        s += w
        if x <= s:
            return item
    return items[-1]

def _gen_line_payload(r: random.Random, target_size: int) -> str:
    # Create a rich single or multi-line payload suitable for // comments.
    # Include Unicode, punctuation, code-like snippets, and various EOLs.
    pieces = []
    # Sometimes prefix with TODO/FIXME tags
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        tag = _weighted_choice(r, ["TODO", "FIXME", "HACK", "NOTE"], [3,2,1,2])
        pieces.append(f" {tag}: ")
    # Add key=value pairs
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        k = _rand_identifier(r)
        v = _rand_identifier(r)
        pieces.append(f"{k}={v} ")
    # Add numbers and hex values
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        pieces.append(f"{r.randint(-2**31, 2**31-1)} ")
        pieces.append(f"0x{r.randint(0, 2**32-1):08x} ")
    # Add some Unicode
    unicode_pool = ["π", "✓", "©", "™", "αβγ", "你好", "👍", "👩‍💻", "résumé", "naïve"]
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        pieces.append(r.choice(unicode_pool) + " ")
    # Add code-ish fragment
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        ident1 = _rand_identifier(r)
        ident2 = _rand_identifier(r)
        op = r.choice(["=", "+=", "-=", "*=", "/=", "|=", "&=", "^="])
        pieces.append(f"{ident1} {op} {ident2}; ")
    # Possibly include JSON-looking snippet
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        pieces.append('{"key": "value", "n": 123} ')
    # Join initial chunk
    s = "".join(pieces)
    # Add random filler with safe characters for comments
    safe_chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "
    # Introduce some newlines to create multiple // lines
    while len(s.encode('utf-8')) < target_size:
        # Occasionally add a newline with various EOLs
        if r.random() < 0.2:
            s += r.choice(LINE_ENDINGS)
        else:
            s += r.choice(safe_chars)
    return s

def _gen_block_payload(r: random.Random, target_size: int) -> str:
    # Create text that intentionally avoids the "*/" sequence.
    # We allow newlines and a wide range of characters but will sanitize any
    # accidental terminator sequence.
    base_chunks = []
    # Add a brief description line
    base_chunks.append(" Block comment payload ")
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        base_chunks.append(f"section:{_rand_identifier(r)} ")
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        base_chunks.append(f"ver={r.randint(0, 100)} ")
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        base_chunks.append("tags=[alpha,beta,gamma] ")
    s = "".join(base_chunks)

    # Allowed characters; we will sanitize occurrences of '*/'
    pool = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " \t"
    # Introduce structured lines separated by newlines
    while len(s.encode('utf-8')) < target_size:
        if r.random() < 0.25:
            s += r.choice(LINE_ENDINGS)
            # occasional indented bullet
            if r.random() < 0.5:
                s += "  - " + _rand_identifier(r) + ": " + _rand_identifier(r) + " "
        else:
            s += r.choice(pool)
    # Sanitize: replace any occurrence of */ with * / to keep comment open until fuzzer adds closing */
    s = s.replace("*/", "* /")
    return s

def _choose_size(r: random.Random) -> int:
    # Choose a size aiming for variety but within 1..(MAX_SIZE-10) to leave room
    # for the fuzzer's prefixes/suffixes.
    choices = [32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048]
    weights = [5, 6, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2]
    size = int(_weighted_choice(r, list(map(str, choices)), weights))
    return min(size, MAX_SIZE - 16)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Decide whether to target line or block comment scenario by crafting a payload
    # suitable for both, but with bias to block-safe (since line can include anything).
    target_size = _choose_size(r)
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        payload = _gen_line_payload(r, target_size)
    else:
        payload = _gen_block_payload(r, target_size)

    # Ensure UTF-8 encodable; Python strings are Unicode; encode to bytes.
    b = payload.encode('utf-8', errors='strict')
    # Enforce max size
    if len(b) > MAX_SIZE:
        b = b[:MAX_SIZE]
    return b
